credentials.description: Notch Pay private key, sent as is in Authorization and in X-Grant, for transfers, beneficiaries, balance and webhooks

example_prompt: Update a Notch Pay webhook endpoint to change its URL or the list of subscribed events.

url.description: New HTTPS URL for the webhook endpoint.

events.description: New list of event types to subscribe to. Replaces the existing events list entirely.

description.description: New human-readable label for this webhook endpoint.

parameters.name: endpoint
parameters.description: The webhook endpoint ID to update.

gotchas: Updating the events field replaces the entire list — it is not a merge. To add a single event type, fetch the current list via get_webhook first, append the new event, then send the full updated array.
The endpoint path parameter is the webhook endpoint ID, not its URL.
At least one body field (url, events, or description) must be provided; sending an empty body may return a 422.
The new URL must be HTTPS. HTTP URLs are rejected.

Authorization takes the key as is, with no 'Bearer ' prefix. Which key goes there is unsettled: Notch Pay's Authentication page shows the public key in it next to X-Grant (`-H "Authorization: YOUR_PUBLIC_KEY"` `-H "X-Grant: YOUR_PRIVATE_KEY"`), while this spec sends the private key, following its earlier note that a public key returns 406 Not Acceptable (not stated in the docs). See open_questions before relying on either.

This endpoint also requires the `X-Grant` header carrying your private key (`X-Grant: YOUR_PRIVATE_KEY`). Without it Notch Pay returns 403 "This endpoint requires additional authentication"; a wrong value returns 403 "Invalid grant key".
open_questions: Notch Pay's docs show `Authorization: YOUR_PUBLIC_KEY` together with `X-Grant: YOUR_PRIVATE_KEY` on this endpoint, while this spec sends the private key in Authorization (see the gotcha about 406 with a public key). Which key Authorization must carry when X-Grant is present is not confirmed.
